notes.meaning: Amos was a herdsman, so he speaks like one. Bashan had rich pastures and fat, strong cattle. He calls the rich people of Samaria 'cows of Bashan' because they lived in luxury and pushed the weak around, like big cattle goring small ones. They crushed the poor to pay for their feasts and their drinking.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Keil and Delitzsch say most modern commentators take the 'cows' to be the wealthy wives of Samaria. In this reading they push their husbands to fund their drinking, as the BSB wording suggests.

notes.meaning: God makes a solemn promise, sworn by His holiness. Because He is holy, He cannot let this wrong go on. Enemies, the Assyrian army, will drag these people away like fish pulled out of water on hooks. Their children will go too, down to the very last one.

When Samaria falls, its walls will be broken open. The proud people will rush out through the gaps, each one straight ahead, with no time to look around. They will be thrown out into exile. The word 'Harmon' is unclear. It may be a place they are taken to, or it may refer to a palace or high place.

God speaks with sharp irony: 'Go on, keep sinning at your shrines!' Bethel and Gilgal were places of false worship that God had not chosen. The people copied the rules of true worship. They gave many sacrifices and tithes (a tenth of their goods) and loudly announced their gifts. But they did it their own way, without obeying God, so it only added to their sin. Commentators differ on the leavened bread. Some say it broke God's law. Others say it was allowed, and the real problem was the wrong place and their own invented worship.

'Cleanness of teeth' means there was no food to eat. God had sent famine on their towns as a warning. He wanted them to come back to Him. But they did not return. This sad refrain repeats five times in the chapter and shows both their stubbornness and God's patient love.

God held back the spring rain just when the crops needed it most. Rain fell on one town or field but not on the one next to it. This showed it was God's hand and not chance. Thirsty people stumbled from town to town for water and still did not get enough. Yet they did not turn back to God. Matthew Henry adds that people often run from one thing to another looking for satisfaction, but will not come to God, who alone can satisfy.

Next God struck their crops with blight and mildew. Locusts ate their gardens, vines, fig trees and olive trees. These troubles echo the warnings God gave in the law of Moses. Calvin notes that the weather and harvests are not ruled by chance but by God. Still the people did not return.

God sent disease like the plagues of Egypt, and war that killed their young men. Their horses were taken or destroyed. So many lay dead that the smell of the camps filled their noses. God had once struck Egypt to save Israel. Now He was treating Israel like an enemy, yet they still did not return.

Some of Israel was destroyed as badly as Sodom and Gomorrah, cities God wiped out for their sin. Those who survived were like a burning stick pulled from the fire just in time. God spared a remnant (a small group) out of mercy and because of His covenant promise. Even this narrow escape did not bring them back to Him.

Since nothing else has worked, God will now bring a worse judgment. He does not say exactly what, which makes the warning even more serious. 'Prepare to meet your God' can be heard as a challenge: who could stand against Him in battle? Most of these commentators also hear a call to repent: humbly turn to God and ask His forgiveness before it is too late. Matthew Henry applies it to us too: we must meet God now through Christ, before we face Him as Judge.

Amos shows how great the God they must meet really is. He made the mountains and the wind. He knows people's secret thoughts and shows them what is in their hearts. He rules day and night and walks over the high places of the earth. His name is the LORD, the God of Hosts, the one all heaven's armies obey. So it is foolish to fight Him and wise to make peace with Him.
